why: THE CANVAS, LOCALLY (P6.d): 'whats been down?' composed in the canvas vocabulary from the reads recorded on 2026-09-20 (mine.json). Blocks, arrangement and prose are the session's. NO MODEL TURN WAS SPENT.
question: whats been down?
answer:
Down is **one shop, and its whole fall is a single Monday.**

OPUS gave back more than the estate lost in total; four shops went the other way. Day against the same weekday, OPUS is level or ahead everywhere but that Monday. The one to act on is Greenhills: more people in, less spent each, four named lines gave back most of what they earned - an empty shelf, seen from the till. Stock cannot confirm it.

Shall I pull those four lines day by day?

blocks.question: Is the estate down?
blocks.claim: Less than the week before, and one shop is more than all of it

blocks.question: Which shops?
blocks.claim: Three down, four up, and OPUS is nearly all of it

blocks.question: Is OPUS in decline, or was one day unusual?
blocks.claim: Its whole fall is one Monday, against a Monday unlike any other
blocks.thought: Each day against the same weekday before it; both weekend days are ahead.

blocks.question: Which lines, at Greenhills?
blocks.claim: Four named lines gave back most of what they earned

blocks.question: Does the stock record back that up?
blocks.claim: It cannot - yesterday's crossings are at other shops
blocks.thought: No low-stock level is set anywhere; none of these is at Greenhills.

children.say: Which leaves one shop that is genuinely losing ground, and it is not the one with the big number.

reading.claim: one shop, and its whole fall is a single Monday
reading.caveat: 132 of 523 compared lines have no usable baseline, so the ranked fallers understate how much simply stopped selling. The windows are the closed week 7-13 Sep against 31 Aug-6 Sep; the stock crossings are yesterday. No low-stock level has ever been set, so a line is only visible the day it reaches zero.
